admission_apply.text: You trace the rim. Three sides agree. The fourth is shorter by a hair you cannot pinch.

native.admission_inspect: A palm-sized horn plate, ruled with one square. The four edges look equal until the light shifts.
apply_texts: Held flat, the four sides agree. The ease fades as soon as the plate is tilted.
One last pass. The corner you trusted is only a crease. The square does not correct itself.
The same four marks. Their order has shifted by one corner, and the gap has moved with them.
The short side lengthens when you look away, then fails again under the thumb.
You trace the rim. Three sides agree. The fourth is shorter by a hair you cannot pinch.
inspect_texts: A palm-sized horn plate, ruled with one square. The four edges look equal until the light shifts.
A thin square of pale horn. One corner is sharp; the opposite corner reads as a short blunt line.
Fine lines cross the square and continue to the rim, then stop. Nothing beyond the rim is marked.
The horn square is warm. Three edges meet; the fourth stops short, as if the plane ended early.
The square corner has been counted twice. Both counts fit the marks. Neither explains the gap.
Warm horn, cold lines. You count three sides, then four, and both counts stop at the rim.
native.name: Skew Square
